Graph data: structures, conversion, and batching

Source: vignettes/graph-data.Rmd
graph-data.Rmd
library(graphlearnR)

Every model in graphlearnR consumes the same data structure, a graph_data object. This article explains what it stores, the rules it enforces, and how to get your data into it.

The data model

A graph with N nodes and E stored edges has

field shape meaning
x N x F matrix node features
edge_index 2 x E integer matrix row 1 source, row 2 target, 1-based
y length N node labels (factor or numeric)
edge_attr E x D matrix edge features
edge_weight length E scalar edge weights
edge_y length E edge labels
graph_y length 1 graph label
train_mask, val_mask, test_mask length N logical node splits
node_ids length N original identifiers
edge_pair length E pair id of each stored edge (undirected graphs) 
g <- graph_data(
  x = matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE),
  edge_index = rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)),
  y = factor(c("a", "b", "a")),
  edge_weight = c(0.5, 2)
)
g
#> <graph_data> directed graph: 3 nodes, 2 edges
#>   node features [3 x 2]
#>   edge weights
#>   node labels: factor with 2 levels

Indexing is 1-based

Node 1 is the first row of x. Edge index matrices, seeds for sampling, node pairs for link prediction, and every returned node id use the same convention. The only place a 0-based index appears is at an explicit boundary with other software, through to_zero_based() and from_zero_based().

to_zero_based(g$edge_index)
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    0    1
#> [2,]    1    2

Direction

An edge (i, j) sends a message from i to j; layers aggregate over the incoming edges of each node. A directed graph is stored as given.

For an undirected graph, give each pair once. graphlearnR stores both directions next to each other and records the pair id. Edge level fields such as weights are copied to both directions.

u <- graph_data(edge_index = rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)), edge_weight = c(1, 5),
                directed = FALSE)
u$edge_index
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    1    2    2    3
#> [2,]    2    1    3    2
u$edge_weight
#> [1] 1 1 5 5
u$edge_pair
#> [1] 1 1 2 2
num_edges(u)
#> [1] 4
num_edges(u, unique_pairs = TRUE)
#> [1] 2

Giving both directions of an undirected pair is almost always a mistake, so it raises a warning.

w <- graph_data(edge_index = rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 1)), directed = FALSE)
#> Warning: Undirected input contains reciprocal pairs (both u-v and v-u). Supply
#> each undirected edge once, or use `directed = TRUE` if the list already holds
#> both directions.

Validation

graph_data() validates its input and fails with a message that names the problem: out of range or fractional indices, missing values, mismatched lengths, and overlapping masks.

try(graph_data(edge_index = rbind(1, 5), num_nodes = 3))
#> Error : Invalid graph_data:
#> * `edge_index` refers to nodes outside 1:3 (first bad edge: column 1, 1 -> 5).
try(graph_data(x = diag(2), train_mask = c(TRUE, FALSE), test_mask = c(TRUE, FALSE)))
#> Error : Invalid graph_data:
#> * `train_mask` and `test_mask` overlap.

validate_graph() runs the same checks on an object you have modified by hand.

Inspecting a graph 

k <- dataset_karate()
c(nodes = num_nodes(k), edges = num_edges(k), features = num_node_features(k))
#>    nodes    edges features 
#>       34      156       34
has_self_loops(k)
#> [1] FALSE
has_isolated_nodes(k)
#> [1] FALSE
head(degree(k))
#> [1] 16  9 10  6  3  4

Conversion

From and to igraph

from_igraph() reads vertex names into node_ids, the weight edge attribute into edge_weight, and any attributes you name into features.

ig <- igraph::make_graph("Zachary")
igraph::V(ig)$age <- seq_len(igraph::vcount(ig))
gi <- from_igraph(ig, x_attrs = "age")
gi
#> <graph_data> undirected graph: 34 nodes, 156 edges (78 undirected pairs)
#>   node features [34 x 1]
back <- to_igraph(gi)
igraph::ecount(back)
#> [1] 78

An undirected igraph object becomes an undirected graph_data; the round trip keeps the edge count.

From an edge list

Real data rarely numbers nodes 1:N. graph_from_edgelist() maps arbitrary identifiers through an optional node table, which also supplies features and labels. Nodes that appear in the table but in no edge are kept as isolated nodes.

edges <- data.frame(from = c("ann", "bob", "cat"), to = c("bob", "cat", "ann"),
                    strength = c(3, 1, 2))
nodes <- data.frame(id = c("ann", "bob", "cat", "dan"), age = c(31, 45, 27, 52),
                    group = c("x", "y", "x", "y"))
ge <- graph_from_edgelist(edges, nodes = nodes, feature_cols = "age",
                          label_col = "group", weight_col = "strength")
ge
#> <graph_data> directed graph: 4 nodes, 3 edges
#>   node features [4 x 1]
#>   edge weights
#>   node labels: factor with 2 levels
ge$node_ids
#> [1] "ann" "bob" "cat" "dan"
edgelist_from_graph(ge)
#>   from  to weight
#> 1  ann bob      3
#> 2  bob cat      1
#> 3  cat ann      2

From an adjacency matrix

Dense and sparse (Matrix) adjacency matrices both work. A symmetric matrix gives an undirected graph unless directed = TRUE. Entry A[i, j] is the edge from i to j.

A <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = c(1, 2, 3), j = c(2, 3, 1), x = c(1, 2, 3), dims = c(3, 3))
ga <- graph_from_adjacency(A)
ga$edge_index
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    1    2    3
#> [2,]    2    3    1
adjacency_from_graph(ga)
#> 3 x 3 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>           
#> [1,] . 1 .
#> [2,] . . 2
#> [3,] 3 . .

To tensors

graph_tensors() converts every field to a torch tensor on a chosen device: features to floating point, indices and class labels to long, and masks to bool. Indices stay 1-based, which is what R torch indexing expects.

tt <- graph_tensors(k)
tt
#> <graph_tensors> 34 nodes, 156 edges on cpu
tt$edge_index$dtype
#> torch_Long

Many graphs: batching

Graph level tasks train on many small graphs. graph_batch() joins them into one disconnected graph: node indices are offset so no edge crosses between graphs, and batch records which graph each node belongs to.

gs <- dataset_synthetic_graphs(3, seed = 1)
b <- graph_batch(gs)
b
#> <graph_batch> 3 graphs, 25 nodes, 64 edges
b$node_ptr
#> [1]  0  5 14 25
table(b$batch)
#> 
#>  1  2  3 
#>  5  9 11

unbatch() reverses the operation exactly.

parts <- unbatch(b)
identical(parts[[2]]$edge_index, gs[[2]]$edge_index)
#> [1] TRUE

Datasets

graph_dataset() wraps a list of graphs and applies an optional transform when a graph is accessed. write_graph_dataset() and graph_dataset_disk() keep large collections on disk, one file per graph, loading each on demand.

ds <- graph_dataset(dataset_synthetic_graphs(20, seed = 2),
                    transform = add_degree_features)
ds
#> <graph_dataset> 20 graphs
ncol(ds[[1]]$x)
#> [1] 2

Public benchmark datasets are downloaded, not bundled, and their MD5 checksum is verified before use. download_tu_dataset("MUTAG") reads a TU Dortmund graph classification dataset and download_planetoid_raw("cora") reads the raw LINQS release of Cora; read their licenses before redistributing them.

Transforms

Transforms are plain functions from a graph to a graph, so they compose with compose_transforms() or with the native pipe.

g2 <- graph_data(x = diag(3), edge_index = rbind(c(1, 1, 2), c(2, 2, 3)))
g2 |> coalesce_edges() |> add_self_loops() |> (\(h) h$edge_index)()
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5]
#> [1,]    1    2    1    2    3
#> [2,]    2    3    1    2    3
ks <- split_nodes(dataset_karate("degree"), seed = 1)
head(normalize_features(ks, stats_mask = ks$train_mask)$x)
#>             [,1]
#> [1,]  2.19650230
#> [2,]  0.69645195
#> [3,]  0.91074486
#> [4,]  0.05357323
#> [5,] -0.58930550
#> [6,] -0.37501259

Pass stats_mask to normalize_features() to compute centering and scaling statistics from training nodes only, so test information does not leak into the features.
